readings: For each product (`product_id` on the order items), count the order-item lines. Give each product a share: its count divided by the sum over all products. Then take the plain average of those shares across products. For the products whose share is strictly above that average, return a single unrounded row with: their combined count, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds the overall average share.
queries:
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT product_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM Order_Items
  GROUP BY product_id
),
shares AS (
  SELECT product_id, cnt, CAST(cnt AS REAL) / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM counts) AS share
  FROM counts
),
avg_share AS (
  SELECT AVG(share) AS a FROM shares
)
SELECT SUM(cnt) AS combined_count,
       AVG(share) AS average_share,
       AVG(share - (SELECT a FROM avg_share)) AS average_excess
FROM shares
WHERE share > (SELECT a FROM avg_share);
